node_identity_trap_evidence.resolution: board_signature=0x1e950f (atmega328p) confirms this is the Uno, NOT the Leonardo's 0x1e9587 (atmega32u4) -- the signature probe is what actually proves identity here, not the node name or its timestamp alone; the timestamp is corroborating evidence that a real board swap occurred between the two sessions.
node_identity_trap_evidence.trap: The node NAME /dev/ttyACM0 is IDENTICAL to the one the Leonardo used in plan 160-10 -- but this is a DIFFERENT PHYSICAL BOARD. Node creation timestamp is the only distinguishing evidence available, since the name alone is reused.

operator_declared_board: Uno (ATmega328P) with the Rev 2.0 RURP shield mounted
operator_probe_agreement_note: Operator declared the Uno (ATmega328P); the avrdude signature probe independently identified connected_part=atmega328p via board_signature=0x1e950f (the known-good value for the Uno, probe_board.py's _SIGNATURE_TO_MCU table -- and explicitly NOT 0x1e9587/atmega32u4, the Leonardo used in the immediately prior plan 160-10 on the IDENTICAL node name /dev/ttyACM0, nor 0x1e9516/atmega328pb). The two agree; the plan's stop-and-report clause was not triggered.
